attributes.board_name: Maine Board of Licensure in Medicine

rules.accepted_credit_types: Category 1 CME from programs sponsored by organizations accredited by the AMA, ACCME or the Maine Medical Association CME committee; also credit for peer-reviewed articles, posters, teaching in AMA Cat 1 activities, degrees, postgraduate training (per Board Rule Ch. 1 §11)
rules.new_licensee_rule: CME is prorated during the first licensure period.
rules.alternatives: Current ABMS certification, including maintenance of certification, is deemed equivalent to the 40 hours (lifetime certification is not). Opioid CME still required.
rules.audit_note: Licensee affirms CME at renewal; board staff perform random audits. Extension/deferment up to 6 months for illness or hardship.

topics.who: All physicians, whether or not they prescribe opioids (Category 1)

rules.notes: Biennial renewal by the last day of the birth month (odd/even year matches birth year). Board jurisprudence exam every other renewal (~4 years). From 1/1/2027 MD and DO boards merge into the Maine Board of Medicine (32 M.R.S. ch. 153); CME rules may change.
rules.legal_basis: 02-373 C.M.R. Ch. 1, Section 11; Joint Rule Ch. 21 (opioid CME); 32 M.R.S. §3280-A

rules.accepted_credit_types: CME designated Category 1 or 2 by the AOA, ACGME or AMA; at least 40 hours must be osteopathic medical education (primary care: AOA Category 1; specialists: AOA, ACGME or AMA Category 1)
rules.audit_note: Evidence appended or certified on a board form at renewal; random audit of 10% of licensees in odd-numbered years, proof due within 30 days.
rules.alternatives: Waiver or extra time by petition for illness, hardship or military service. Board may not require specialty certification or OCC.
rules.notes: DOs are licensed by the Maine Board of Osteopathic Licensure (maine.gov/osteo). Rule Ch. 14 dates from 1999 and refers to reporting by January 1 of even years; renewal schedule unclear. Boards merge 1/1/2027 (32 M.R.S. ch. 153). No fee at 70+.
rules.legal_basis: 32 M.R.S. §2581; 02-383 C.M.R. Ch. 14; Joint Rule Ch. 21
